characterization_methods.key_findings: The 17Al alloy aged at 625 °C for 1 h exhibited a Vickers hardness of 813.0 ± 20.8 HV.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load of 9.8 N for 15 s; 5 repeated measurements per sample, values given as the average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the aged 17Al sample, including the 625 °C/1 h condition.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: For 17Al at 625 °C/1 h the SE panel shows a uniform matrix with fine 'New precipitates' (magenta-labelled) revealed in a magnified inset.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol); 50 µm main-panel scale bars with small insets
characterization_methods.purpose: Image the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn and new precipitates) in the aged 17Al alloy, including the 625 °C/1 h condition (Fig. 8).

interfaces.interface_notes: Direct TEM/EDS of β-Mn interfaces was performed on the 17Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 6 h (Fig. 12), not on the 625 °C/1 h condition; the interface description here is based on the general mechanism reported for the ultra-hard alloys of the same series.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α (BCC) matrix → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase, as proposed for the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys during aging (b0068); for 17Al at 625 °C/1 h the α→β-Mn transformation is essentially complete.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (at.%, x = 15, 17, 19) ingots produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials using a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere; the 17Al alloy refers to the alloy with 17 at.% Al (nominal Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu).
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
After homogenization the ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
The rolled plates were cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (this is the parent solution-treatment state proc_st-1100c-10min-oq of the 17Al alloy).
The solution-treated 17Al sample was aged at 625 °C for 1 h, followed by water quenching — this defines the specific aged sample (17Al, 625 °C, 1 h).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times, value is the average of 5 measurements

precipitates.distribution: within the β-Mn / at the β-Mn interfaces

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 625 °C for 1 h, the α (BCC) matrix of the 17Al alloy had almost completely transformed into β-Mn; numerous fine precipitates (later identified by EBSD as BCC and FCC Cu-rich phases) were distributed within the β-Mn. The solution-treated base state of the alloy is a single α (BCC) phase.

unmapped_findings: The solution-treated (parent-state) 17Al alloy had a Vickers hardness of 259.8 ± 1.5 HV, which serves as the common baseline for all 17Al aging conditions including the 625 °C/1 h sample.

For the 17Al alloy, aging at 625 °C produced a nearly time-independent hardness plateau of ~813–878 HV across 1–10 h (813.0 ± 20.8 HV at 1 h, 872.0 ± 24.4 HV at 3 h, 878.4 ± 28.3 HV at 6 h, 870.5 ± 24.9 HV at 10 h); the peak hardness of the 17Al alloy (924.9 ± 25.8 HV) was instead reached at 575 °C for 6 h, not at 625 °C.

The specific sample (17Al aged at 625 °C for 1 h) is not the peak-hardness state of the 17Al alloy; the nanoindentation measurements (Fig. 13) and TEM observations (Fig. 12) of the 17Al alloy were performed on the 575 °C/6 h peak-hardness sample, and the XRD trace for 17Al (Fig. 10) was measured on the 575 °C/1 h sample, so those results do not directly correspond to this 625 °C/1 h sample.
